ns2:section.sectionText: ELECTRONIC STRUCTURE OF CONDENSED MATTER. The study of the electronic structure of materials is at a momentous stage, with new algorithms and computational methods, and rapid advances in basic theory. Many properties of materials can now be determined directly from the fundamental equations for the electrons, providing new insights into critical problems in physics, chemistry, and materials science. PHYS 598SCM will provide a unified exposition of the basic theory and methods of electronic structure, together with instructive examples of practical computational methods and real-world applications. The course will include density functional theory - with emphasis upon understanding the ideas, practical methods, and limitations - and practical calculations with open source codes. There will be a focus upon important developments such as "Car-Parrinello simulations" and the theory of localization in terms of Berry's phases. The primary resource will be the book, "Electronic Structure Basic Theory and Practical Methods" by R. M. Martin, Cambridge University Press, 2004, (http://books.cambridge.org/0521782856.htm), with additional material on important many-body methods such as quantum Monte Carlo and dynamical mean field theory. An integral part of the course will be a project done by each student individually or as part of a team; the topic can be on an aspect of electronic structure theory or on an application of an existing method to a problem in physics, chemistry, or materials science. Links to related resources can be found at ElectronicStructure.org and at the Materials Computation Center.
